question: As per a news report in March 2022, scientists at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS) designed an electrocatalyst system for energy-efficient production of ________ with the help of electrolysis of urea.
solution:
The correct answer is __**hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Scientists at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS) have designed an electrocatalyst system for the energy-efficient production of hydrogen.
 
• This production of hydrogen is achieved through the electrolysis of urea, which is more energy-efficient compared to water electrolysis.
 
• Hydrogen is a clean fuel and has the potential to be a significant part of the renewable energy landscape.
 
• The development of efficient and cost-effective methods for hydrogen production is crucial for the advancement of hydrogen energy technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrogen:**

 
 
• Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe and is considered a potential clean energy carrier for the future.
 
• It can be used in fuel cells to generate electricity, with water as the only byproduct, making it environmentally friendly.
 
• Hydrogen can be produced from various sources, including natural gas, biomass, and water, through different processes such as steam methane reforming, gasification, and electrolysis.
 
• Research and development in hydrogen production aim to make the process more efficient and cost-effective to promote its use as a sustainable energy source.
 
 
 
• **Electrolysis of Urea:**
 
 
• Urea electrolysis is a process that involves the decomposition of urea into hydrogen, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide using an electric current.
 
• This process is more energy-efficient compared to water electrolysis because urea has a lower thermodynamic potential for decomposition.
 
• Urea is commonly available as a waste product in agricultural and industrial processes, making it a cost-effective feedstock for hydrogen production.
 
• The development of effective electrocatalysts for urea electrolysis is crucial for enhancing the efficiency and feasibility of this method.
 
 
 
• **Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS):**
 
 
• CeNS is an autonomous research institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India.
 
• The institute focuses on research in the areas of nano and soft matter sciences, including the development of novel materials and technologies.
 
• CeNS aims to address scientific and technological challenges through innovative research and collaboration with academic and industrial partners.
 
• The development of the electrocatalyst system for hydrogen production is one of the many significant contributions of CeNS in the field of renewable energy.
